execution.note: Several agents share one M5 GPU; bandwidth_control readings are reported per artifact to expose contention.

accepted: Tiled row-IFFT store for the scalar 512 loss path (engine.py:4607-4636 with plumbing at engine.py:2041 and engine.py:2917): 22.767 to 21.055 ms on the isolated stage pair, 404.0 to 369.5 ms end-to-end, bit-exact on three parameter triples.
Nothing new was accepted for the fit path: both named levers are closed by measurement (see leverage_ceilings).
findings.bottleneck_verdict: The 8937-BF fit is device_memory-traffic bound at the machine's streaming ceiling: the batch-2 objective moves 84.376 GB in 647.0 ms = 130.4 GB/s and the batch-1 objective 46.892 GB in 360.8 ms = 130.0 GB/s, against a same-session mx.array copy control of 126.3-132.3 GB/s. No sync, host round-trip, geometry or chunk-size term is measurable above noise.
findings.fit_change_verdict: f357069 (tiled scalar row IFFT) does not touch the fit objective path: a 4-trial fit calls _reconstruct_prepared 0 times and the batched row IFFT 1944 times (= 18 packs x 108 objectives), and the batched path was already tiled in the frozen tree. The paired fit A/B therefore shows only host drift (79.28 -> 77.72 s p50) while both objective paths are equal within noise (batch2 648.3 vs 647.0 ms, batch1 360.8 vs 359.2 ms). The change is an interactive redraw/scalar-loss win, not a fit win.
findings.fit_split_at_8937_bf: Fit wall 79.03 s = 200-trial loop 65.9 s (83.4%, 100 batch-2 calls at p50 653.3 ms = 3.06 candidates/s) + Nelder-Mead 11.4 s (14.4%, 31 batch-1 calls at p50 367.6 ms = 2.72 evals/s) + initial loss 0.44 s (0.6%) + final object/phase 0.52 s (0.7%); optuna bookkeeping adds 0.4 s (0.6%).

leverage_ceilings.batch_the_200_trials: Already batch-2 (engine.py:4924). Wider batches are re-tiled into pairs (engine.py:4955-4966) and the code records a measured 2.8x per-candidate regression at batch 4, so K=4 buys 0%. The arithmetic ceiling is the G share: 11.1% of per-candidate traffic at K=2, so K=4 would cap at 5.6% and K=infinite at 11.1% of the trial loop, i.e. 9.2% of the fit.
leverage_ceilings.reduce_intermediate_bytes: Measured closed: the plane is a full 2.10 MB complex64 buffer with no exact symmetry (4.5-7.1% mirror residuals, |imag|/|real| = 0.036) and any fusion would have to hold a whole plane on-chip against a 32 KB threadgroup limit.

ranked_bottlenecks: engine.py:4975 (pair pack loop) -> engine.py:2626 (tiled row store) -> engine.py:2337 (tiled column load): the row-IFFT intermediate round trip is 4.295 GB of the 4.834 GB moved per 512-BF pair pack (88.9%), i.e. 37.48 GB of the 42.19 GB per candidate at batch 2. It is 86% of the fit wall.

engine.py:2660/2712 (G_qk read inside the row kernel) + engine.py:4834 (_pk_batch_from_prepared): the 9.408 GB half-plane G cache is 20.1% of a batch-1 candidate (9.41 GB) and 11.1% at batch 2 (4.70 GB/candidate).
engine.py:5080 (_nelder_mead_refine): 31 sequential batch-1 evaluations = 14.4% of the fit; each is one 46.89 GB objective, so the G read cannot be amortised across the simplex.

engine.py:3013 (per-element geometry) and engine.py:2438 (atan2 column stage): ablating sqrt+sincos from the row IFFT moves that stage 8% and ablating atan2 from the column stage moves it 5%, so compute is exposed but small.

engine.py:2958 (mx.eval per pack in the pair loop): 18 syncs per objective, required to bound the 2.15 GB pack buffers; measured depth A/B shows deeper pipelining is slower (391.5/397.5/399.5/481.5 ms at k=1..4).
rejected: Fusing the row and column stages: the only remaining structural lever (2.686 GB down to 0.539 GB per pack) but it needs a threadgroup-transposed 2D kernel with new parity validation, so it is out of scope for this audit.

Enabling the SIMD register transpose column stage on non-M5-Max hardware: bit-exact and 4.3% faster on that stage, but it changes a hardware-gated kernel path for devices that cannot be measured on this host.
Smaller or larger phase-loss chunk (512 to 256/1024): changes the float32 reduction grouping and is not bit-exact; measured 388-437 ms against 370-402 ms at 512.
Removing the per-chunk mx.eval: measured slower and higher peak memory.
Reducing the pair pack eval depth or re-packing BF boundaries: no peak-memory saving (MLX caches freed buffers) and slower batch2 (1028.1 ms at depth 1 vs 697.8 ms at depth 5).

Hoisting the per-element geometry into a table like the native Metal ssb_precompute_cross_trig: a per-(bf, row, col) table is 75 GB, and the separable form is a different float32 expression, so it cannot be bit-exact.

Hoisting the per-candidate geometry into a Metal-style cross_trig table: indexed by (row, col, bf) it is ~75 GB; a (dx, dy)-indexed table would need new per-element index arithmetic and still only recovers part of the measured 8%/5% ablation, so the payoff does not survive the bit-exactness cost.
Batching Nelder-Mead evaluations: the simplex is sequential and speculative reflect+expand batching would add wasted candidates for a <=5.6% amortisation of the smallest term in the fit.

verdict_on_suspected_causes.chunk_size_cliff: not on this 24 GB host: 512 BF is the measured optimum, and 1024 is not bit-exact.
verdict_on_suspected_causes.fit_host_round_trips: negligible: 7 evals and one host read per objective out of ~350 ms; the fit is 131 objective calls and nothing else.
verdict_on_suspected_causes.memory_or_compute_bound: memory bound at the ceiling (129-134 GB/s of a 125-130 GB/s copy ceiling), unlike the native Metal probe at 42 GB/s.
verdict_on_suspected_causes.per_chunk_sync: refuted twice: fewer syncs are slower and use more memory.
verdict_on_suspected_causes.repeated_geometry: real in the native Metal sense but not hoistable here without changing the float32 expression.

Paired A/B (bandwidth_control 129.9/124.3 GB/s): flat row+column stage pair 22.767 ms vs tiled 21.055 ms (1.081x), end-to-end scalar loss 404.0 ms vs 369.5 ms (1.093x), both bit-exact; column-stage simd transpose 8.635 ms vs 9.026 ms (1.043x) and bit-exact; pair objective with simd 351.97 ms vs 360.93 ms.

artifact_results.intermediate-redundancy: Real 512x512 complex64 row-IFFT plane, 2,097,152 B: no exact redundancy. Joint (q,c)->(512-q,512-c) mirror residual 45,715 = 4.8% of peak 954,211, row mirror 4.5%, column mirror 7.1%, max|imag|/max|real| 0.0356, so the plane cannot be halved or stored as real without approximation. De-tiled copy of the tiled store equals the flat store bit-exactly (max abs err 0.0) and the flat plane sha256 is identical across engines.
